   102	
   103	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: the continuous trapezoid
   104	`s ↦ max 0 (min 1 ((n+1) min(s-p, q-s)))`, which increases to the indicator of `(p,q)`. -/
   105	def trap (n : ℕ) (p q s : ℝ) : ℝ := max 0 (min 1 (((n : ℝ) + 1) * min (s - p) (q - s)))
   106	
   107	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: the trapezoid is continuous. -/
   108	theorem trap_continuous (n : ℕ) (p q : ℝ) : Continuous (trap n p q) :=
   109	  continuous_const.max (continuous_const.min (continuous_const.mul
   110	    ((continuous_id.sub continuous_const).min (continuous_const.sub continuous_id))))
   111	
   112	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: `0 ≤ trap ≤ 1`. -/
   113	theorem trap_mem (n : ℕ) (p q s : ℝ) : 0 ≤ trap n p q s ∧ trap n p q s ≤ 1 :=
   114	  ⟨le_max_left _ _, max_le zero_le_one (min_le_left _ _)⟩
   115	
   116	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: the trapezoid vanishes off `(p,q)`. -/
   117	theorem trap_eq_zero {n : ℕ} {p q s : ℝ} (hs : s ∉ Ioo p q) : trap n p q s = 0 := by
   118	  have hm : min (s - p) (q - s) ≤ 0 := by
   119	    rw [mem_Ioo, not_and_or, not_lt, not_lt] at hs
   120	    rcases hs with h | h
   121	    · exact (min_le_left _ _).trans (by linarith)
   122	    · exact (min_le_right _ _).trans (by linarith)
   123	  have h : ((n : ℝ) + 1) * min (s - p) (q - s) ≤ 0 :=
   124	    mul_nonpos_of_nonneg_of_nonpos (by positivity) hm
   125	  unfold trap
   126	  exact max_eq_left ((min_le_right _ _).trans h)
   127	
   128	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: the trapezoid has compact support. -/
   129	theorem trap_hasCompactSupport (n : ℕ) (p q : ℝ) : HasCompactSupport (trap n p q) :=
   130	  HasCompactSupport.intro (isCompact_Icc (a := p) (b := q)) fun _ hs =>
   131	    trap_eq_zero fun h => hs (Ioo_subset_Icc_self h)
   132	
   133	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: `trap n p q s → 1_{(p,q)}(s)` for every `s`. -/
   134	theorem trap_tendsto (p q s : ℝ) :
   135	    Tendsto (fun n => trap n p q s) atTop (𝓝 ((Ioo p q).indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) s)) := by
   136	  by_cases hs : s ∈ Ioo p q
   137	  · rw [indicator_of_mem hs]
   138	    set m := min (s - p) (q - s) with hmdef
   139	    have hm : 0 < m := lt_min (by linarith [hs.1]) (by linarith [hs.2])
   140	    obtain ⟨K, hK⟩ := exists_nat_gt (1 / m)
   141	    refine tendsto_const_nhds.congr' ?_
   142	    filter_upwards [eventually_ge_atTop K] with n hn
   143	    have hKn : (K : ℝ) ≤ n := by exact_mod_cast hn
   144	    have h1 : 1 ≤ ((n : ℝ) + 1) * m := by
   145	      have : 1 / m < (n : ℝ) + 1 := by linarith
   146	      rw [div_lt_iff₀ hm] at this
   147	      linarith
   148	    have : trap n p q s = 1 := by
   149	      unfold trap
   150	      rw [← hmdef, min_eq_left h1, max_eq_right zero_le_one]
   151	    exact this.symm
   152	  · rw [indicator_of_notMem hs]
   153	    simp only [trap_eq_zero hs]
   154	    exact tendsto_const_nhds

   158	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: the index `min(⌊(N+1)s⌋, N)` of the cell of `s` among
   159	the `N+1` equal cells of `[0,1]`. -/
   160	def idx (N : ℕ) (s : ℝ) : Fin (N + 1) :=
   161	  ⟨min ⌊((N : ℝ) + 1) * s⌋₊ N, Nat.lt_succ_of_le (min_le_right _ _)⟩
   162	
   163	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: the cell index is measurable. -/
   164	theorem idx_measurable (N : ℕ) : Measurable (idx N) := by
   165	  have h : idx N = (fun k : ℕ => (⟨min k N, Nat.lt_succ_of_le (min_le_right _ _)⟩ :
   166	      Fin (N + 1))) ∘ (fun s : ℝ => ⌊((N : ℝ) + 1) * s⌋₊) := rfl
   167	  rw [h]
   168	  exact measurable_from_nat.comp (Nat.measurable_floor.comp (measurable_const_mul _))
   169	
   170	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: the left node of the cell of `s ∈ [0,1]` is within
   171	`1/(N+1)` of `s`. -/
   172	theorem idx_close {N : ℕ} {s : ℝ} (hs : s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) :
   173	    |s - ((idx N s : ℕ) : ℝ) / ((N : ℝ) + 1)| ≤ 1 / ((N : ℝ) + 1) := by
   174	  set k := ⌊((N : ℝ) + 1) * s⌋₊ with hk
   175	  have hN : (0 : ℝ) < N + 1 := by positivity
   176	  have hx0 : 0 ≤ ((N : ℝ) + 1) * s := mul_nonneg hN.le hs.1
   177	  have hk1 : (k : ℝ) ≤ ((N : ℝ) + 1) * s := Nat.floor_le hx0
   178	  have hk2 : ((N : ℝ) + 1) * s < k + 1 := Nat.lt_floor_add_one _
   179	  have hj : ((idx N s : ℕ) : ℝ) = ((min k N : ℕ) : ℝ) := rfl
   180	  have h1 : ((min k N : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ ((N : ℝ) + 1) * s :=
   181	    (Nat.cast_le.2 (min_le_left _ _)).trans hk1
   182	  have h2 : ((N : ℝ) + 1) * s ≤ ((min k N : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1 := by
   183	    rcases le_total k N with h | h
   184	    · rw [min_eq_left h]; linarith
   185	    · rw [min_eq_right h]; nlinarith [hs.2]
   186	  rw [hj, abs_le]
   187	  constructor
   188	  · have : ((min k N : ℕ) : ℝ) / ((N : ℝ) + 1) ≤ s := by rw [div_le_iff₀ hN]; linarith
   189	    have : 0 ≤ 1 / ((N : ℝ) + 1) := by positivity
   190	    linarith
   191	  · rw [sub_le_iff_le_add, ← add_div, le_div_iff₀ hN]
   192	    linarith
   193	
   194	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: off the nodes `k/(N+1)`, `s ∈ (0,1)` lies in the open
   195	cell `(j/(N+1), (j+1)/(N+1))` exactly when its index is `j`. -/
   196	theorem idx_eq_iff {N : ℕ} {s : ℝ} (hs : s ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1)
   197	    (hnode : ∀ k : ℕ, ((N : ℝ) + 1) * s ≠ k) (j : Fin (N + 1)) :
   198	    idx N s = j ↔
   199	      s ∈ Ioo (((j : ℕ) : ℝ) / ((N : ℝ) + 1)) ((((j : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1) / ((N : ℝ) + 1)) := by
   200	  have hN : (0 : ℝ) < N + 1 := by positivity
   201	  set x := ((N : ℝ) + 1) * s with hx
   202	  have hx0 : 0 ≤ x := mul_nonneg hN.le hs.1.le
   203	  have hx1 : x < (N : ℝ) + 1 := by rw [hx]; nlinarith [hs.2]
   204	  have hkN : ⌊x⌋₊ ≤ N := by
   205	    have h : (⌊x⌋₊ : ℝ) < (N : ℝ) + 1 := (Nat.floor_le hx0).trans_lt hx1
   206	    have h' : ⌊x⌋₊ < N + 1 := by exact_mod_cast h
   207	    omega
   208	  have hval : (idx N s : ℕ) = ⌊x⌋₊ := min_eq_left hkN
   209	  rw [Fin.ext_iff, hval, Nat.floor_eq_iff hx0, mem_Ioo, div_lt_iff₀ hN, lt_div_iff₀ hN,
   210	    mul_comm s]
   211	  constructor
   212	  · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩
   213	    exact ⟨lt_of_le_of_ne h1 (fun h => hnode _ h.symm), h2⟩
   214	  · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩
   215	    exact ⟨h1.le, h2⟩

   217	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: Lebesgue-a.e. `s` is off every node `k/(N+1)`. -/
   218	theorem ae_offNode (N : ℕ) : ∀ᵐ s ∂(volume : Measure ℝ), ∀ k : ℕ, ((N : ℝ) + 1) * s ≠ k := by

   221	  filter_upwards [Measure.ae_ne volume ((k : ℝ) / ((N : ℝ) + 1))] with s hs h
   222	  apply hs
   223	  rw [eq_div_iff (by positivity)]
   224	  linarith

   300	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: for a unit test `g` and `0 ≤ h ≤ M`,

   302	theorem mean_pair_bound {V : Rd d → ℝ} {M : ℝ} (hV : ∀ x, 0 ≤ V x ∧ V x ≤ M)
   303	    {g : Rd d → ℝ} (hg : IsUnitTest g) (hi : Integrable (fun x => V x * g x ^ 2) volume) :
   304	    0 ≤ ∫ x, V x * g x ^ 2 ∧ ∫ x, V x * g x ^ 2 ≤ M := by
   305	  have hsqt := SpatialFourLinear.isTest_sq (φ := g) ⟨hg.1, hg.2.1⟩
   306	  have hsq : Integrable (fun x => g x ^ 2) volume :=
   307	    hsqt.1.continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport hsqt.2
   308	  refine ⟨integral_nonneg fun x => mul_nonneg (hV x).1 (sq_nonneg _), ?_⟩
   309	  calc ∫ x, V x * g x ^ 2 ≤ ∫ x, M * g x ^ 2 :=
   310	        integral_mono hi (hsq.const_mul M) fun x =>
   311	          mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hV x).2 (sq_nonneg _)
   312	    _ = M := by rw [integral_const_mul, hg.2.2, mul_one]

   314	/-- **The Cauchy-Schwarz bound for the finite-cell field** (auxiliary to the Lean route; the
   315	final display of `L:occupation-raw-square`, `integrated_occupation_ceiling.tex` lines 38-41,
   316	`⟨Ψ,ρ_g⟩ ≤ √(v_Ψ A(g))` in its integral form, for the step field `g`).  Under `H:homog` with

   318	`∫_0^1 ∫ h_{Ψ,s} g_s² dx ds ≤ √(v_Ψ A(g))`.  Route (not the TeX's map `Q` and `ρ_g ∈ H_I`):
   319	the cell indicators are limits of continuous trapezoids `χ_j^n`; for the continuous fields
   320	`Φ_n = ∑_j χ_j^n f_j²` the bound is `SpaceTimePositivity.integral_mean_mul_le_sqrt` (wave
   321	item L8-c1); both sides pass to the limit by dominated convergence (the left in time with
   322	bound `(N+1) M`, the right on `(0,1)²` with bound `|s-t|^{-a} ∑ |B_Γ(f_i², f_j²)|`), and the
   323	limits are `∫∫ h g²` and `A(g)`. -/
   324	theorem step_mean_le_sqrt {alpha a : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
   325	    (hH : HomogCovariance d alpha a Γ μ) (hΓ0 : Γ ≠ 0) {Ψ : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ} (hΨ : Ψ ∈ CPos d)

   328	      Real.sqrt (rawCost a Γ Ψ * A a Γ (stepG N f)) := by
   329	  have := hH.Γ_radon
   330	  have ha0 := hH.alpha0_pos
   331	  have ha1 := hH.alpha0_lt_one
   332	  obtain ⟨M, CΨ, hM, hCΨ, -, -, hbd, hlipx, -, hpot⟩ :=
   333	    VariationalMean.variational_global_mean_paper hH hΓ0 hΨ

     4	Retain all original models and amplitudes, put $a = \alpha_0$, $q = 4-\alpha >
     5	2$, $k = 3-\alpha = q-1 > 1$ and $m = q/k$. The temporal kernel is $K(s,t) =
     6	|s-t|^{-a}$ on $I = (0,1)$; its diagonal value may be set to zero. Let
     7	$\mathcal{O}$ be the full strongly $H^1$-measurable unit-profile class defined
     8	before Proposition~\ref{P:occupation-physical-class}. Here we use the
     9	\emph{original} kernel, defining
    10	\begin{equation}\label{E:raw-occupation-definitions}
    11	  \begin{aligned}
    12	    A(g)&=\int_{I^2}K(s,t)B_\Gamma(g_s^2,g_t^2)\ud s\ud t,\\
    13	    C_{\rm occ}&=\sup_{g\in\mathcal{O}}
    14	    \frac{A(g)}{T(g)^{\alpha/2}},&
    15	    \mathcal{E}_\zeta^{\mathcal{O}}
    16	    &=\sup_{g\in\mathcal{O}}\{A(g)-\zeta T(g)\},\qquad \zeta>0.
    17	  \end{aligned}
    18	\end{equation}
    19	The scalar penalty $\zeta$ is not a spatial mask. These objects differ from the
    20	earlier damped-kernel energy. Assume $\Gamma \ne 0$ until the direct zero case
    21	below.

    23	\begin{lemma}[Full-profile squares in the original space]
    24	  \label{L:occupation-raw-square}
    25	  There is a continuous map $Q:H^1(\R^d;\R) \to H_{\mathrm{sp}}$ with
    26	  \[
    27	    \langle Q(f),Q(h)\rangle_{H_{\mathrm{sp}}}
    28	    =B_\Gamma(f^2,h^2),\qquad
    29	    \|Q(f)\|^2=A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f).
    30	  \]
    31	  For $g \in \mathcal{O}$, the element $\rho_g = J_{H_{\mathrm{sp}}}(s\mapsto
    32	  Q(g_s))$ belongs to the original $H_I$ and satisfies
    33	  \begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-raw-identities}
    34	    \|\rho_g\|_{H_I}^2=A(g),\qquad
    35	    \langle\Psi,\rho_g\rangle_{H_I}
    36	    =\int_I\int_{\R^d}h_{\Psi,s}(x)g_s(x)^2\ud x\ud s
    37	  \end{equation}
    38	  for every $\Psi \in \mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{pos}}$. In particular,
    39	  \[
    40	    \langle\Psi,\rho_g\rangle_{H_I}\le\sqrt{v_\Psi A(g)}.
    41	  \]
    42	\end{lemma}
    43	
    44	\begin{proof}
    45	  Approximate $f$ in $H^1$ by real compact smooth $f_n$.
    46	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear} gives
    47	  \[
    48	    \|f_n^2-f_l^2\|_{H_{\mathrm{sp}}}^2
    49	    =C_4(f_n-f_l,f_n+f_l,f_n-f_l,f_n+f_l)
    50	    \le R_{\mathrm{sp}}N(f_n-f_l)^2N(f_n+f_l)^2\to0.
    51	  \]
    52	  Here $N$ is continuous on $H^1$ and $N(f) \le \|f\|_{H^1}$. Completeness
    53	  defines $Q(f)$; interlacing two approximating sequences proves independence.
    54	  Passing the physical four-linear continuity and Hilbert pairings to limits
    55	  proves the first identities. The same difference bound, first for smooth
    56	  approximants and then by passage to the limit, proves continuity of $Q$.
    57	
    58	  Thus, $F_g(s) = Q(g_s)$ is strongly measurable. Writing $b_s = \|\nabla
    59	  g_s\|_2^2$, the unit norm and $0 < \alpha/2 < 1$ give
    60	  \[
    61	    \int_I\|F_g(s)\|^2\ud s
    62	    \le R_{\mathrm{sp}}\int_I b_s^{\alpha/2}\ud s
    63	    \le R_{\mathrm{sp}}T(g)^{\alpha/2}<\infty .
    64	  \]
    65	  Lemma~\ref{L:positive-raw-embedding} now constructs $\rho_g$ and identifies
    66	  its squared norm with the physical $A(g)$. Joint measurability and
    67	  representative independence follow from the continuous physical pairing on
    68	  $(H^1)^2$. Absolute time integrability follows from the same Schur bound.
    69	
    70	  Choose one compact smooth $\chi$ equal to one on all spatial supports of
    71	  $\Psi_t$. For real $f \in H^1$, smooth approximation gives
    72	  \[
    73	    \langle\Psi_t,Q(f)\rangle_{H_{\mathrm{sp}}}
    74	    =\lim_n B_\Gamma(\Psi_t,f_n^2)
    75	    =C_4(\chi,\Psi_t,f,f)=B_\Gamma(\Psi_t,f^2).
    76	  \]
    77	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear} justifies these absolute integrals and
    78	  limits. Polarizing~\eqref{E:positive-bochner-inclusion} gives
    79	  \[
    80	    \langle\Psi,\rho_g\rangle
    81	    =\int_{I^2}K(s,t)\langle\Psi_t,Q(g_s)\rangle_{H_{\mathrm{sp}}}
    82	    \ud t\ud s .
    83	  \]
    84	  The absolute integrand is bounded by the product of two $H_{\mathrm{sp}}$
    85	  norms against $K$, integrable by Schur and $L^2$ Cauchy--Schwarz. Evenness of
    86	  $\Gamma$ and Tonelli for the nonnegative physical integrands
    87	  yield~\eqref{E:occupation-raw-identities}. Hilbert Cauchy--Schwarz with
    88	  $\|\Psi\|^2 = v_\Psi$ proves the bound. No rough occupation is inserted into a
    89	  stochastic flow. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:occupation-raw-square}.
    90	\end{proof}
    91	
    92	\begin{proposition}[Original occupation energy and dilation]
    93	  \label{P:raw-occupation-energy}
    94	  With $K_0 = 2^a/(1-a)$,
    95	  \[
    96	    0<C_{\rm occ}\le K_0R_{\mathrm{sp}}<\infty .
    97	  \]
    98	  Moreover,
    99	  \begin{align}
   100	    \mathcal{E}_\zeta^{\mathcal{O}}
   101	    &=D_\zeta C_{\rm occ}^{2/(2-\alpha)},&
   102	    D_\zeta&=\frac{2-\alpha}{2}
   103	    \left(\frac{\alpha}{2\zeta}\right)^{\alpha/(2-\alpha)},
   104	    \label{E:raw-occupation-energy}\\
   105	    C_{\rm occ}
   106	    &=\left(\frac{2\mathcal{E}_\zeta^{\mathcal{O}}}{2-\alpha}\right)^{(2-\alpha)/2}
   107	    \left(\frac{2\zeta}{\alpha}\right)^{\alpha/2}.
   108	    \label{E:raw-occupation-ratio}
   109	  \end{align}
   110	  In particular, $\mathcal{E}_\zeta^{\mathcal{O}} > 0$ is finite and equals
   111	  $\zeta^{-\alpha/(2-\alpha)}\mathcal{E}_1^{\mathcal{O}}$.
   112	\end{proposition}
   113	
   114	\begin{proof}
   115	  A unit $H^1$ profile has positive gradient energy: a zero weak gradient makes
   116	  it constant, and an $L^2$ constant on $\R^d$ is zero. Hence, $0 < T(g) <
   117	  \infty$. Spatial covariance Cauchy--Schwarz gives $B_\Gamma(g_s^2,g_t^2) \le
   118	  R_{\mathrm{sp}}b_s^{\alpha/4}b_t^{\alpha/4}$. Schur with row bound $K_0$, then
   119	  concavity, proves
   120	  \begin{equation}\label{E:raw-occupation-bound}
   121	    0\le A(g)\le K_0R_{\mathrm{sp}}T(g)^{\alpha/2}.
   122	  \end{equation}
   123	  A fixed compact smooth unit profile, constant in time, belongs to
   124	  $\mathcal{O}$ and has positive $A$ by Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear}.
   125	  This proves positivity and finiteness of $C_{\rm occ}$.
   126	
   127	  The map $(U_\ell g)_s(x) = \ell^{d/2}g_s(\ell x)$ is an $H^1$ isomorphism
   128	  preserving unit mass and strong measurability. It has inverse $U_{1/\ell}$ and
   129	  is a bijection on $\mathcal{O}$. The physical Radon change of variables gives
   130	  \[
   131	    A(U_\ell g)=\ell^\alpha A(g),\qquad
   132	    T(U_\ell g)=\ell^2T(g).
   133	  \]
   134	  Indeed, the two densities contribute $\ell^{2d}$, $\ud x$ contributes
   135	  $\ell^{-d}$, and the pushforward of $\Gamma$ contributes $\ell^{\alpha-d}$.
   136	  Approximation extends the identity to full $H^1$. Taking the union over
   137	  $g,\ell$ leaves the class unchanged. For fixed $A,T > 0$, the derivative of
   138	  $A\ell^\alpha-\zeta T\ell^2$ has the sign of $\alpha A-2\zeta
   139	  T\ell^{2-\alpha}$. Its global maximum occurs at $\ell = (\alpha A/(2\zeta
   140	  T))^{1/(2-\alpha)}$ and equals $D_\zeta[A/T^{\alpha/2}]^{2/(2-\alpha)}$. For
   141	  $A = 0$ the supremum is zero as $\ell\downarrow0$. Bounding every ratio by
   142	  $C_{\rm occ}$ gives one inequality in~\eqref{E:raw-occupation-energy}. Fixed
   143	  ratios approaching its positive supremum give the other by continuity of the
   144	  positive power. Algebra gives~\eqref{E:raw-occupation-ratio} and the penalty
   145	  scaling. No optimizer or minimax interchange is assumed. This proves
   146	  Proposition~\ref{P:raw-occupation-energy}.
   147	\end{proof}
   148	
   149	\begin{lemma}[Countable Rayleigh near-occupations]
   150	  \label{L:occupation-rayleigh-selection}
   151	  For fixed $\Psi \in \mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{pos}}$ and every $\varepsilon > 0$
   152	  there is $g_\varepsilon \in \mathcal{O}$ such that
   153	  \begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-rayleigh-selection}
   154	    I_\Psi^2+T(g_\varepsilon)
   155	    \le\sqrt{v_\Psi A(g_\varepsilon)}+\varepsilon .
   156	  \end{equation}
   157	\end{lemma}
   158	
   159	\begin{proof}
   160	  The real $H^1$ space is separable, for example by its isometric embedding
   161	  $f\mapsto(f,\nabla f)$ into a finite product of $L^2$ spaces. Compact smooth
   162	  density therefore supplies a countable real family. Discard zero and normalize
   163	  each member in $L^2$ to obtain $f_j$ dense in the $L^2$-unit $H^1$ class.
   164	  Normalization preserves convergence because the approximating $L^2$ norms tend
   165	  to one. Put $b_j = \|\nabla f_j\|_2^2$ and $R_j(s) = \int
   166	  h_{\Psi,s}f_j^2-b_j$. Bounded-potential form continuity and
   167	  Proposition~\ref{P:variational-unmasked-rate} give $\lambda_{\Psi,s}^2 =
   168	  \sup_jR_j(s)$. The canonical functions are measurable, indeed continuous. Let
   169	  $U_j = \{s:R_j(s)>\lambda_{\Psi,s}^2-\varepsilon\}$, $A_1 = U_1$ and $A_j =
   170	  U_j\setminus\bigcup_{i<j}U_i$. These first-index cells are Borel and cover
   171	  $I$. Put $g_\varepsilon(s) = f_j$ on $A_j$. Finite-valued truncations using
   172	  $f_1$ on the remaining cells converge pointwise in $H^1$, proving strong
   173	  measurability. A null-set representative may be filled by $f_1$.
   174	
   175	  With $H_\Psi = \sup_{s,x}h_{\Psi,s}(x) < \infty$, the selection implies
   176	  \[
   177	    b(g_\varepsilon(s))
   178	    <\int h_{\Psi,s}g_\varepsilon(s)^2-\lambda_{\Psi,s}^2+\varepsilon
   179	    \le H_\Psi+\varepsilon .
   180	  \]
   181	  Thus, it belongs to the $\mathcal{O}$. Integrating the near-Rayleigh
   182	  inequality, using Lemma~\ref{L:occupation-raw-square}, gives
   183	  \[
   184	    \int_I\lambda_{\Psi,s}^2\ud s+T(g_\varepsilon)
   185	    \le\langle\Psi,\rho_{g_\varepsilon}\rangle+\varepsilon
   186	    \le\sqrt{v_\Psi A(g_\varepsilon)}+\varepsilon .
   187	  \]
   188	  Time Cauchy--Schwarz on the unit interval gives $I_\Psi^2 \le
   189	  \int_I\lambda_{\Psi,s}^2\ud s$. This
   190	  proves~\eqref{E:occupation-rayleigh-selection}. No eigenvector, continuum
   191	  selector or limiting occupation is required. This proves
   192	  Lemma~\ref{L:occupation-rayleigh-selection}.
   193	\end{proof}

   195	For $0 \le b < q/2$ define $F_b(0) = 0$ and
   196	\begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-scalar-map}
   197	  F_b(z)=k\left[
   198	  \frac{(q-2b)^{(q-2b)/2}}{8(q-b)^{q-b}}
   199	  \left(\frac{2z}{2-\alpha}\right)^{(2-\alpha)/2}
   200	  \right]^{1/k},\qquad z>0.
   201	\end{equation}
   202	At $b = 0$ this is exactly the map in~\eqref{E:spatial-static-energy-score}. The
   203	display parameter $b$ does not change the temporal exponent $a$.

   205	\begin{theorem}[The computed occupation ceiling]\label{T:intrinsic-occupation-ceiling}
   206	  For every variational value over nonnegative controls coefficient
   207	  $\mathfrak{c}$,
   208	  \begin{align}
   209	    S_{\mathfrak{c}}^{\mathrm{pos}}
   210	    &\le U_{\mathfrak{c}}
   211	    :=\mathfrak{c}^m k
   212	    \left[\frac{\alpha^{\alpha/2}C_{\rm occ}}{8q^{q/2}}\right]^{1/k}
   213	    \label{E:occupation-score-ceiling}\\
   214	    &=\mathfrak{c}^m(2\zeta)^{\alpha/(2k)}
   215	    F_0(\mathcal{E}_\zeta^{\mathcal{O}}),\qquad \zeta>0.\notag
   216	  \end{align}
   217	  In particular, the original moment constant satisfies $C_2(\Gamma,a) \le U_2$
   218	  for every original model. This ceiling is not asserted to be attained or equal
   219	  to $C_2$.
   220	\end{theorem}
   221	
   222	\begin{proof}
   223	  Fix $\Psi$ and write $v = v_\Psi$, $C = C_{\rm occ}$ and $\beta = \alpha/4$.
   224	  Lemma~\ref{L:occupation-rayleigh-selection} gives $I_\Psi^2 \le
   225	  \sqrt{vC}T^\beta-T+\varepsilon$ for some $T > 0$. Bound it by the supremum
   226	  over all $T \ge 0$ before sending $\varepsilon\downarrow0$. If $v = 0$, that
   227	  supremum is zero. If $v > 0$, the derivative $\beta\sqrt{vC}T^{\beta-1}-1$
   228	  strictly decreases from infinity to $-1$. Its unique positive zero is $T_* =
   229	  (\beta\sqrt{vC})^{1/(1-\beta)}$. The global maximum equals
   230	  $(q/4)(\alpha/4)^{\alpha/q}(vC)^{2/q}$. In both cases,
   231	  \[
   232	    I_\Psi\le Dv^{1/q},\qquad
   233	    D=\sqrt{q/4}(\alpha/4)^{\alpha/(2q)}C^{1/q}.
   234	  \]
   235	  The scalar function $\mathfrak{c} Dv^{1/q}-v/2$ vanishes at zero, tends to
   236	  minus infinity, and has strictly decreasing derivative. Its unique positive
   237	  maximum is at $v_* = (2\mathfrak{c} D/q)^{q/k}$, with value $kv_*/2$. Direct
   238	  positive-power algebra gives
   239	  \[
   240	    (2D/q)^q=q^{-q/2}(\alpha/4)^{\alpha/2}C .
   241	  \]
   242	  Since $k+\alpha = 3$, the maximum is precisely $U_{\mathfrak{c}}$
   243	  in~\eqref{E:occupation-score-ceiling}, with denominator eight. Substitution
   244	  of~\eqref{E:raw-occupation-ratio} gives the second form, retaining the factor
   245	  $(2\zeta)^{\alpha/(2k)}$. Take the supremum over the smooth positive-control
   246	  class. Theorem~\ref{T:intrinsic-second-moment} identifies $C_2 =
   247	  S_2^{\mathrm{pos}}$, proving the moment ceiling. The penalty factor cancels
   248	  its energy scaling, so the ceiling is independent of $\zeta$. This proves
   249	  Theorem~\ref{T:intrinsic-occupation-ceiling}.
   250	\end{proof}
   251	
   252	\begin{corollary}[A common spatial-energy bracket]
   253	  \label{C:intrinsic-spatial-bracket}
   254	  With the same original covariance and $M_a$
   255	  of~\eqref{E:temporal-equilibrium-mass},
   256	  \begin{equation}\label{E:intrinsic-spatial-bracket}
   257	    2^m M_a^{-1/k}F_0(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}})
   258	    \le C_2(\Gamma,a)
   259	    \le2^m K_0^{1/k}F_0(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}).
   260	  \end{equation}
   261	  For $\Gamma \ne 0$ there is also the comparison of the energies defined here
   262	  \[
   263	    C_2\le2^mF_0(\mathcal{E}_{1/2}^{\mathcal{O}})
   264	    <2^mF_a(\mathcal{E}_{1/2}^{\mathcal{O}}).
   265	  \]
   266	\end{corollary}
   267	
   268	\begin{proof}
   269	  Insert $C_{\rm occ} \le K_0R_{\mathrm{sp}}$ into
   270	  \eqref{E:occupation-score-ceiling} and use \eqref{E:spatial-energy-map}. This
   271	  gives the upper bracket; the lower is \eqref{E:spatial-static-energy-score}
   272	  multiplied by $2^m$, using Theorem~\ref{T:intrinsic-second-moment}. Both
   273	  concern one common spatial energy, not an assumed first moment.
   274	
   275	  For completeness put
   276	  \[
   277	    \Delta=\tfrac12[q\log q+(q-2a)\log(q-2a)]
   278	    -(q-a)\log(q-a)>0.
   279	  \]
   280	  Here $a > 0$ and $q-2a > 2-a > 1$. The scalar inequality for the difference of
   281	  logarithms applies at exactly these conditions, without $q \ge 3$.
   282	  Equivalently the strict midpoint convexity of $x\log x$ on positive arguments,
   283	  whose second derivative is $1/x$, gives the sign. Subtracting logarithms
   284	  in~\eqref{E:occupation-scalar-map} gives
   285	  \[
   286	    \log(F_a(z)/F_0(z))=\Delta/k,\qquad
   287	    \frac{\mathfrak{c}^mF_a(\mathcal{E}_\zeta^{\mathcal{O}})}{U_{\mathfrak{c}}}
   288	    =\exp\!\left(\frac{\Delta-(\alpha/2)\log(2\zeta)}{k}\right).
   289	  \]
   290	  At $\zeta = 1/2$ this and the ceiling prove the strict comparison. At $\zeta =
   291	  1$ the comparison is not universally favorable. For $\alpha = 5/4,a = 1/2,d =
   292	  2$,
   293	  \[
   294	    8[\Delta-(\alpha/2)\log2]
   295	    =\log\frac{11^{11}7^7}{2^5 9^{18}}<0,
   296	  \]
   297	  since $11^{11}7^7 = 234966429149994773$ and $2^5 9^{18} =
   298	  4803028329503971872$. This contrasts computed bounds; it refutes no moment
   299	  inequality. This proves Corollary~\ref{C:intrinsic-spatial-bracket}.
   300	\end{proof}
   301	
   302	For $\Gamma = 0$, all original means and variational values vanish and $C_2 =
   303	0$. Here $Q = 0$, $A = 0$ and $C_{\rm occ} = 0$. The supremum of $-\zeta T(g)$
   304	is zero: dilate a fixed unit compact profile by $\ell^{d/2}f(\ell x)$ and let
   305	$\ell\downarrow0$. The same argument gives $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}} = 0$ and
   306	the earlier damped energy zero, without using a zero vector as a unit profile.
   307	With $F_b(0) = 0$, every non-strict bound above is the zero identity. These
   308	energies are not identified with Chen's printed energies.

    54	    ∫ x, φ x ∂Γ =

    58	covariance is a nonnegative, even, positive-definite tempered Radon measure
    59	`Γ` on `ℝ^d` with positive even tempered Radon spectral measure `μ`,
    60	`Γ = ∫ e^{i ξ·x} μ(dξ)`; for every Borel set `A` and `c > 0`,
    61	`Γ(cA) = c^{d-α} Γ(A)`; `α₀ + α < 2` (`E:threshold`), with `0 < α < d` or
    62	`α = d = 1`. A Lean measure is nonnegative, and on `ℝ^d` a locally finite
    63	Borel measure is a Radon measure. -/
    64	structure HomogCovariance (d : ℕ) (alpha alpha0 : ℝ) (Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)) :
    65	    Prop where
    66	  dim : d = 1 ∨ d = 2 ∨ d = 3
    67	  alpha0_pos : 0 < alpha0
    68	  alpha0_lt_one : alpha0 < 1
    69	  Γ_radon : IsLocallyFiniteMeasure Γ
    70	  Γ_even : IsEven Γ
    71	  Γ_tempered : IsTempered Γ
    72	  Γ_posdef : IsPosDefDistr Γ
    73	  μ_radon : IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ
    74	  μ_even : IsEven μ
    75	  μ_tempered : IsTempered μ
    76	  spectral : IsSpectralMeasure Γ μ
    77	  scaling : ∀ A : Set (Rd d), MeasurableSet A → ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c →
    78	    Γ (c • A) = ENNReal.ofReal (c ^ ((d : ℝ) - alpha)) * Γ A
    79	  threshold : alpha0 + alpha < 2
    80	  alpha_range : (0 < alpha ∧ alpha < d) ∨ (alpha = d ∧ d = 1)

    83	(with `a = α₀`). -/
    84	theorem homog_params {d : ℕ} {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
    85	    (h : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) :

    87	  ⟨h.dim, h.alpha0_pos, h.alpha0_lt_one, by linarith [h.threshold], h.alpha_range⟩
    88	
    89	/-- `E:kappa` with the manuscript's hypothesis: under `H:homog`,
    90	`κ = (4 - α - α₀)/(3 - α) ∈ (1, 2)`. -/
    91	theorem kappa_mem_Ioo_paper {d : ℕ} {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
    92	    (h : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) :
    93	    KappaRange.kappa alpha alpha0 ∈ Set.Ioo 1 2 :=
    94	  KappaRange.kappa_mem_Ioo d alpha alpha0 h.dim h.alpha0_pos h.alpha0_lt_one
    95	    h.threshold h.alpha_range
    96	
    97	/-- `E:driver-parameters` with the manuscript's hypothesis (the section
    98	retains `H:homog` and sets `a = α₀`): its strict intervals are nonempty. -/
    99	theorem parameters_nonempty_paper {d : ℕ} {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
   100	    (h : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) :
   101	    ∃ γ θ β : ℝ, (0 < γ ∧ γ < min (1 / 2) ((2 - alpha) / 2)) ∧
   102	      (1 / 2 < θ ∧ θ < β ∧ β < min (1 - alpha0 / 2) ((3 - alpha0 - alpha) / 2)) :=
   103	  DriverParameters.parameters_nonempty d alpha alpha0 (homog_params h)

     1	\section{Physical spatial pairings and the full occupation class}
     2	\label{S:spatial-occupation-foundation}
     3	
     4	Retain a nonzero original covariance from Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} with its
     5	amplitude. Set $a = \alpha_0$, $k = 3-\alpha > 1$, $q = 4-\alpha = k+1$ and $D =
     6	q-2a > 0$. The scalar $D$ is fixed. All profiles are real. The original positive
     7	temporal exponent and threshold imply $\alpha < 2$; this is the strict
     8	inequality used in the scalar powers and concavity. The finite variational value
     9	over nonnegative controls $S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}$ is that of
    10	Proposition~\ref{P:variational-positive-scores}.
    11	
    12	\begin{lemma}[The physical two-point integral]\label{L:spatial-physical-pair}
    13	  The positive measure $\nu(\ud x,\ud y) = \ud x\,\Gamma(\ud y)$ is
    14	  sigma-finite. For nonnegative functions define
    15	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-physical-pair}
    16	    B_\Gamma(f,h)=\int f(x)h(x-y)\nu(\ud x,\ud y)
    17	  \end{equation}
    18	  initially as an extended nonnegative integral, using finite Borel
    19	  representatives of Lebesgue classes. Its value is representative independent.
    20	  Lebesgue-a.e. convergence transfers to $\nu$-a.e. convergence at both
    21	  positions $x$ and $x-y$.
    22	\end{lemma}
    23	
    24	\begin{proof}
    25	  Local finiteness of $\Gamma$ gives sigma-finiteness on exhausting balls, and
    26	  Lebesgue measure is sigma-finite. If $N$ is Borel and Lebesgue null, Tonelli
    27	  applied first in $x$ gives $\nu\{x\in N\} = 0$ and $\nu\{x-y\in N\} = 0$,
    28	  because every fixed translate of $N$ is null. An arbitrary Lebesgue null set
    29	  has a Borel null superset. Thus, arbitrary versions are measurable in the
    30	  $\nu$ completion with the same value, and the same observation applies to the
    31	  exceptional sets of a.e. convergence. Signed pairings will be used only after
    32	  absolute convergence. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-physical-pair}.
    33	\end{proof}
    34	
    35	Put $A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g) = B_\Gamma(g^2,g^2)$ and $b(g) = \|\nabla g\|_2^2$ on
    36	$H^1$; initially $A_{\mathrm{sp}}$ is used only for smooth compact profiles
    37	before the extension below. For smooth compact $z$, write $U_z = \Gamma*z$ in
    38	its usual pointwise sense.
    39	
   350	\subsection{The kernel row and full occupation energy}
   351	
   352	Define, for $u \ne 0$,
   353	\begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-damped-kernel}
   354	  K_\star(u)=\frac1{\Gamma_E(a)}
   355	  \int_0^\infty
   356	  e^{-(\lambda+\lambda^2/(2D))|u|}
   357	  \lambda^{a-1}\ud\lambda,
   358	\end{equation}
   359	and set $K_\star(0) = 0$ for time integration.
   360	
   361	\begin{lemma}[Exact row maximum]\label{L:occupation-kernel-row}
   362	  The kernel is even, positive off zero, locally integrable, decreasing on
   363	  $(0,\infty)$, and $K_\star(u) \le |u|^{-a}$ off zero. Its exact row maximum on
   364	  $[0,1]$ is
   365	  \begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-kernel-row}
   366	    \max_{s\in[0,1]}\int_0^1K_\star(s-t)\ud t
   367	    =R_\star:=2\int_0^{1/2}K_\star(u)\ud u\in(0,\infty).
   368	  \end{equation}
   369	\end{lemma}
   370	
   371	\begin{proof}
   372	  Dropping the positive quadratic damping bounds the mixture by the Gamma
   373	  integral $|u|^{-a}$. Positivity and monotonicity follow directly from the
   374	  integrand, and $a < 1$ gives local integrability. Put $\Phi(t) =
   375	  \int_0^tK_\star(u)\ud u$. It is concave because its integrand is decreasing on
   376	  positive arguments. The row is $\Phi(s)+\Phi(1-s) \le 2\Phi(1/2)$, with
   377	  equality at $s = 1/2$. The diagonal value changes no time integral. This
   378	  proves Lemma~\ref{L:occupation-kernel-row}.
   379	\end{proof}
   380	
   381	Let $\mathcal{O}$ be the full class of strongly $H^1(\R^d;\R)$-measurable fields
   382	$s\mapsto g_s$ on $(0,1)$ with $\|g_s\|_2 = 1$ a.e. and $T(g) =
   383	\int_0^1b(g_s)\ud s < \infty$. No time smoothness, common compact support or
   384	optimizer condition is imposed.
   385	
   386	\begin{proposition}[The full physical occupation class]
   387	  \label{P:occupation-physical-class}
   388	  The pairings $(s,t)\mapsto B_\Gamma(g_s^2,g_t^2)$ are measurable,
   389	  representative independent and equal to their physical integrals. With
   390	  \[
   391	    J(g)=\int_0^1\int_0^1
   392	    K_\star(s-t)B_\Gamma(g_s^2,g_t^2)\ud s\ud t,
   393	  \]
   394	  every $g \in \mathcal{O}$ satisfies
   395	  \begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-physical-bound}
   396	    0\le J(g)\le R_\star R_{\mathrm{sp}}T(g)^{\alpha/2}<\infty.
   397	  \end{equation}
   398	  The energy over exactly this full class satisfies
   399	  \begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-own-energy}
   400	    0<\mathcal{E}_\star^{\mathcal{O}}
   401	    :=\sup_{g\in\mathcal{O}}\big(J(g)-T(g)/2\big)
   402	    \le R_\star^{2/(2-\alpha)}\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}<\infty.
   403	  \end{equation}
   404	\end{proposition}
   405	
   406	\begin{proof}
   407	  The map $s\mapsto b(g_s)$ is measurable by continuity of the squared gradient
   408	  norm. Also $\int_0^1\|g_s\|_{H^1}^2\ud s = 1+T(g)$. Use a separably valued
   409	  strong representative and replace exceptional null times by one fixed real
   410	  unit compact bump. Joint measurable spatial representatives exist: approximate
   411	  this Bochner $L^2$ field by simple $H^1$-valued functions with summable
   412	  $L^2(0,1;H^1)$ errors, and choose measurable spatial versions for their
   413	  countably many values. A subsequence has a measurable spacetime $L^2$ limit,
   414	  and for a.e. $s$ its spatial $L^2$ class is $g_s$.
   415	  Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-physical-pair} makes every pairing independent of the
   416	  spatial versions. The continuous pairing map on the separable space $H^1\times
   417	  H^1$ from Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear} consequently gives a
   418	  measurable function of $(s,t)$ agreeing a.e. with the nonnegative physical
   419	  integral.
   420	
   421	  Set $F(s) = b(g_s)^{\alpha/4}$. Equations~\eqref{E:spatial-homogeneous-bound}
   422	  and~\eqref{E:spatial-square-CS} give $B_\Gamma(g_s^2,g_t^2) \le
   423	  R_{\mathrm{sp}}F(s)F(t)$. Since $0 < \alpha/2 < 1$, concavity on the unit time
   424	  interval yields $\int_0^1F^2 = \int_0^1b(g_s)^{\alpha/2}\ud s \le
   425	  T(g)^{\alpha/2}$. Now use $2F(s)F(t) \le F(s)^2+F(t)^2$ and the exact row
   426	  bound \eqref{E:occupation-kernel-row}, whose column bound is the same because
   427	  $K_\star$ is even, to obtain \eqref{E:occupation-physical-bound}. Positive
   428	  Tonelli is valid before finiteness is known. Null-time modifications affect
   429	  only a product-null set, so they cannot change $J$.
   430	
   431	  The scalar maximum of $R_\star R_{\mathrm{sp}}T^{\alpha/2}-T/2$ over $T \ge 0$
   432	  is $R_\star^{2/(2-\alpha)}\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}$, by the same
   433	  differentiation as~\eqref{E:spatial-energy-map}. This bounds the occupation
   434	  supremum from above. For positivity take a constant-in-time unit compact
   435	  profile and its spatial dilation $U_\ell$. Its $J$ is $J_0\ell^\alpha
   436	  A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)$, where $J_0 = \int_0^1\int_0^1K_\star(s-t)\ud s\ud t \in
   437	  (0,\infty)$, while $T = \ell^2b(g)$. For sufficiently small $\ell > 0$,
   438	  $\alpha < 2$ makes $J-T/2 > 0$. Thus, the nonempty supremum is a positive
   439	  finite real number. This is a comparison bound; no attaining profile or
   440	  equality in it has been asserted. No spatial point trace or rough stochastic
   441	  evolution was used. This proves Proposition~\ref{P:occupation-physical-class}.
   442	\end{proof}

1	\section{The unmasked Rayleigh rate and nonnegative controls}
     2	\label{S:unmasked-variational}
     3	
     4	Fix a nonzero covariance satisfying Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}, including its
     5	original amplitude, and set $a = \alpha_0$. Define the full class
     6	\begin{equation}\label{E:variational-positive-class}
     7	  \mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{pos}}
     8	  =\{\Psi\in C_c^\infty((0,1)\times\R^d;\R):
     9	  \Psi\ge0,\ \Psi\ne0\}.
    10	\end{equation}
    11	
    12	\input{notes/figures/nonseparable-controls}
    13	It includes nonseparable tests. It is nonempty: if $b(z) = e^{-1/(1-z^2)}$ on
    14	$|z| < 1$ and zero otherwise, then $b(4s-2)\prod_{j=1}^db(x_j)$ belongs to this
    15	class. All boundary derivatives vanish because exponential decay dominates every
    16	power of $(1-z^2)^{-1}$. For each $\Psi$ retain the original mean $h_{\Psi,s}$
    17	and original variance $v_\Psi = \E W(\Psi)^2$ from~\eqref{E:compact-raw-mean}--%
    18	\eqref{E:compact-raw-cost}. Neither the test nor its covariance is changed by a
    19	physical mask. We write $h_s$ when $\Psi$ is fixed.
    20	
    21	\subsection{Global bounds and the unmasked spectral bottom}
    22	
    23	\begin{lemma}[Gaussian envelope for the original covariance]
    24	  \label{L:variational-heat-envelope}
    25	  For the normalized heat kernel $p_\epsilon(x) =
    26	  (2\pi\epsilon)^{-d/2}e^{-|x|^2/(2\epsilon)}$,
    27	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-heat-envelope}
    28	    (\Gamma*p_\epsilon)(x)
    29	    =\int e^{i\xi\cdot x}e^{-\epsilon|\xi|^2/2}\mu(\ud\xi),
    30	    \qquad
    31	    0\le(\Gamma*p_\epsilon)(x)
    32	    \le(\Gamma*p_\epsilon)(0)<\infty.
    33	  \end{equation}
    34	  The value at zero is strictly positive.
    35	\end{lemma}
    36	
    37	\begin{proof}
    38	  A positive tempered Radon measure has polynomial ball growth. Indeed, evaluate
    39	  its tempered bound on a nonnegative smooth cutoff equal to one on $B_1$,
    40	  dilated by $R \ge 1$. Its finitely many Schwartz seminorms are bounded by
    41	  $CR^N$, so positivity gives a ball-mass bound $CR^N$. Summing dyadic annuli
    42	  shows that $(1+|x|)^{-L}$ is integrable for $L > N$. Apply this separately to
    43	  $\Gamma$ and $\mu$. Gaussian weights are therefore integrable against both
    44	  measures. The classical convolution on the left is finite and smooth locally
    45	  in $x$: on compact $x$ sets its translated Gaussian derivatives are bounded by
    46	  any fixed sufficiently fast polynomial weight in the integration variable.
    47	
    48	  Pair the convolution with a Schwartz test $\varphi$. Absolute Fubini is
    49	  justified by these weights. The resulting pairing is that of $\Gamma$ with
    50	  $p_\epsilon*\varphi$. Applying the spectral convention in
    51	  Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} and the identity $\int p_\epsilon(y)e^{-i\xi\cdot
    52	  y}\ud y = e^{-\epsilon|\xi|^2/2}$ gives exactly the right side
    53	  of~\eqref{E:variational-heat-envelope} as a distribution. The heat kernel is
    54	  even, so either Fourier sign gives that same Gaussian multiplier. Its spectral
    55	  integral is absolutely finite and continuous in $x$ by dominated convergence.
    56	  Thus, equality of the two continuous distributions gives equality at every
    57	  $x$, without an extra normalization factor. The physical convolution is
    58	  nonnegative. Evenness of $\mu$ makes the spectral integral real, and its
    59	  absolute value is bounded by its total Gaussian mass, the value at zero.
    60	  Finally, $\Gamma \ne 0$ and $p_\epsilon > 0$ give strict positivity there.
    61	  This proves Lemma~\ref{L:variational-heat-envelope}.
    62	\end{proof}
    63	
    64	\begin{lemma}[Global regularity of the original mean]
    65	  \label{L:variational-global-mean}
    66	  Every mixed time and space derivative of $h_s$ is globally bounded in space,
    67	  uniformly on compact time intervals. In particular, for $I = [0,1]$ there are
    68	  finite constants $M,C_\Psi$ such that
    69	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-global-mean}
    70	    0\le h_s(x)\le M,\qquad
    71	    \|h_s-h_t\|_\infty\le C_\Psi|s-t|,
    72	    \qquad s,t\in I.
    73	  \end{equation}
    74	\end{lemma}
    75	
    76	\begin{proof}
    77	  Extend $\Psi$ by zero in time; its compact support inside $(0,1)$ makes this a
    78	  smooth extension. For any mixed derivative $D\Psi$, a fixed $\epsilon > 0$ and
    79	  compactness of its common spatial support give $|D\Psi(t,x)| \le
    80	  C_Dp_\epsilon(x)$ for all $t,x$. Here the heat kernel has a positive minimum
    81	  on that support. Lemma~\ref{L:variational-heat-envelope} consequently bounds
    82	  $\Gamma*|D\Psi(t,\cdot)|$ uniformly in $t,x$. Ordinary local differentiation
    83	  against the Radon measure gives the corresponding derivatives of the
    84	  convolution. After the change $r = s-t$,
    85	  \[
    86	    h_s(x)=\int_\R |r|^{-a}
    87	    (\Gamma*\Psi(s-r,\cdot))(x)\ud r.
    88	  \]
    89	  For $s$ in a compact interval the relevant $r$ lie in a fixed bounded
    90	  interval. The preceding global bound times $|r|^{-a}$ is integrable since $a <
    91	  1$. Every derivative thus falls on the smooth test and passes through the
    92	  integral by dominated convergence, with the claimed global spatial bounds.
    93	  Nonnegativity follows from positive kernels. The bounded time derivative
    94	  proves the Lipschitz estimate. No directional decay of the mean has been
    95	  inferred. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:variational-global-mean}.
    96	\end{proof}
    97	
    98	\begin{proposition}[The unmasked Rayleigh rate]
    99	  \label{P:variational-unmasked-rate}
   100	  On complex $L^2(\R^d)$, the operator $H_s = -\Delta-h_s$ is self-adjoint on
   101	  $H^2$, with form domain $H^1$ and form $q_s(f) = \|\nabla f\|_2^2-\int
   102	  h_s|f|^2$. Its spectral bottom $E_s$ is uniformly negative on $I$. The
   103	  positive rate $\lambda_{\Psi,s} = \sqrt{-E_s}$ satisfies
   104	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-real-rayleigh}
   105	    \lambda_{\Psi,s}^2
   106	    =\sup_{\substack{f\in H^1(\R^d;\R)\\\|f\|_2=1}}
   107	    \left(\int h_sf^2-\|\nabla f\|_2^2\right).
   108	  \end{equation}
   109	  It is Lipschitz on $I$, and $I_\Psi: = \int_0^1\lambda_{\Psi,s}\ud s$ is
   110	  positive and finite. No eigenstate at the unmasked bottom is asserted.
   111	\end{proposition}
   112	
   113	\begin{proof}
   114	  The Fourier Laplacian $A = -\Delta$ is self-adjoint on $H^2$, being
   115	  multiplication by $|\xi|^2$ with its maximal domain. Multiplication $B_s =
   116	  -h_s$ is bounded self-adjoint with norm at most $M$. Thus, $H_s = A+B_s$ is
   117	  densely defined, symmetric and closed on $H^2$; the two graph norms are
   118	  equivalent under a bounded perturbation. For real $b > M$,
   119	  \[
   120	    H_s-ib=(I+B_s(A-ib)^{-1})(A-ib).
   121	  \]

   124	  \in D(H_s^*)$ solve $(H_s-ib)v = (H_s^*-ib)u$ with $v \in D(H_s)$. Then $u-v
   125	  \in \ker(H_s^*-ib) = \operatorname{Ran}(H_s+ib)^\perp = \{0\}$. Hence,

   130	  \[

   162	  spectral theorem was applied to $H_s$. This proves
   163	  Proposition~\ref{P:variational-unmasked-rate}.

   132	    =\int|\mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)|^2\mu(\ud\xi).

   134	  Both integrals are finite: $c_Q$ is compactly supported and $\Gamma$ is
   135	  Radon, while $|\mathcal{F}_0Q|^2$ is Schwartz and $\mu$ is tempered.
   136	  No density of either measure is required.
   137	
   138	  Since $\|Q\|_1=1$, we have $|\mathcal{F}_0Q|\le1$. Integration by parts
   139	  and the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality give
   140	  \[
   141	    |\xi|\,|\mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)|
   142	    \le\|\nabla Q\|_1
   143	    \le2\|g\|_2\|\nabla g\|_2=2\sqrt b.
   144	  \]
   145	  Splitting into $|\xi|^2\le4b$ and $|\xi|^2>4b$ therefore yields
   146	  \[
   147	    |\mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)|^2\le\frac{8b}{4b+|\xi|^2}.
   148	  \]
   149	  The deterministic resolvent calculation in the proof of
   150	  Lemma~\ref{L:damped-homogeneous-norms}, together
   151	  with~\eqref{E:intro-spectral-mass}, gives, for $q>0$,
   152	  \[
   153	    \mathcal{R}_\Gamma(q):=\int\frac{\mu(\ud\xi)}{q^2+|\xi|^2}
   154	    =q^{\alpha-2}R_\alpha<\infty.
   155	  \]
   156	  Consequently,
   157	  \[
   158	    A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)\le8b\mathcal{R}_\Gamma(2\sqrt b)
   159	    =2^{1+\alpha}R_\alpha b^{\alpha/2}.
   160	  \]
   161	  Nonnegativity follows from the spectral identity. If $\Gamma=0$, then
   162	  $\mu=0$ and both sides of~\eqref{E:spatial-fourier-bound} vanish. This proves
   163	  Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-fourier-bound}.
   164	\end{proof}

   166	\begin{proposition}[The finite smooth spatial ratio]
   167	  \label{P:spatial-smooth-ratio}

   169	  A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)/b(g)^{\alpha/2}$. Its supremum $R_0$ over these profiles is
   170	  a positive finite real number, and
   171	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-smooth-score}
   172	    S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}\ge
   173	    k\left[
   174	    \frac{R(g)\alpha^{\alpha/2}}{8M_aq^{q/2}}
   175	    \right]^{1/k}.
   176	  \end{equation}
   177	\end{proposition}

   179	\begin{proof}
   180	  The gradient energy $b(g)$ is positive: a nonzero $L^2$ function with zero

181	  weak gradient would have Fourier transform supported only at zero, and hence
   182	  would vanish. Its square is nonnegative nonzero smooth compact, so the
   183	  autocorrelation argument in the proof of
   184	  Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-static-controls} gives
   185	  $0 < A:=A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)<\infty$. Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-fourier-bound} gives
   186	  $R(g)\le2^{1+\alpha}R_\alpha$ for every such profile. A normalized compact
   187	  bump supplies a positive ratio. Thus, $0<R_0<\infty$, independently of the
   188	  finiteness of $S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}$. It remains to prove the score inequality.
   189	  With $U_\ell g(x)=\ell^{d/2}g(\ell x)$, the physical changes of variables give
   190	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-dilation}
   191	    A_{\mathrm{sp}}(U_\ell g)=\ell^\alpha A,\qquad
   192	    b(U_\ell g)=\ell^2b(g).
   193	  \end{equation}
   194	  The factors in the first identity are $\ell^{2d}$ from the two squares,
   195	  $\ell^{-d}$ from $\ud x$, and $\ell^{\alpha-d}$ from the Radon pushforward.
   196	
   197	  For $\theta,\ell > 0$ choose the smooth control $z = \theta(U_\ell g)^2$. The
   198	  Rayleigh test $U_\ell g$ gives $\lambda_z(1)^2 \ge \theta\ell^\alpha
   199	  A-\ell^2b$, while $B_\Gamma(z,z) = \theta^2\ell^\alpha A$. For any $L > 0$,
   200	  put $u = \alpha/q > 0$ and choose
   201	  \[
   202	    \ell^2=uL^2/b,\qquad
   203	    \theta=(1+u)L^2/(\ell^\alpha A).
   204	  \]

   206	  gives
   207	  \[
   208	    S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}\ge L-CL^q,\qquad
   209	    C=\frac{M_a(1+u)^2}{2R(g)u^{\alpha/2}}>0.
   210	  \]

   212	  4/q$, $1/(q^qC) = R(g)\alpha^{\alpha/2}/(8M_aq^{q/2})$,

   214	  real value $S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}$ fixed at the start of the section; only the
   215	  proof of $R_0<\infty$ is independent of that input. This proves
   216	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-smooth-ratio}.

   219	\begin{proposition}[The physical four-linear extension]
   220	  \label{P:spatial-four-linear}
   221	  For real $f \in H^1(\R^d)$ define $N(f) = \|f\|_2^{1-\alpha/4}\|\nabla
   222	  f\|_2^{\alpha/4}$. Every physical square pairing is finite and
   223	  \begin{align}
   224	    A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f)&\le R_0N(f)^4,\label{E:spatial-homogeneous-bound}\\
   225	    0\le B_\Gamma(f^2,h^2)
   226	    &\le\sqrt{A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f)A_{\mathrm{sp}}(h)}.
   227	    \label{E:spatial-square-CS}
   228	  \end{align}
   229	  The signed integral $C_4(f_1,f_2,f_3,f_4) = B_\Gamma(f_1f_2,f_3f_4)$ is
   230	  absolutely convergent and jointly continuous on $(H^1)^4$, with
   231	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-four-linear}
   232	    \int|f_1(x)f_2(x)f_3(x-y)f_4(x-y)|\ud\nu
   233	    \le R_0\prod_{j=1}^4N(f_j).
   234	  \end{equation}

   236	  $R_0$. Every nonzero $H^1$ profile has $A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f) > 0$.

   238	
   239	\begin{proof}
   240	  For smooth compact $f$, normalization in $R_0$ proves
   241	  \eqref{E:spatial-homogeneous-bound}, including $f = 0$. All exponents in $N$
   242	  are positive and $N(f) \le \|f\|_{H^1}$. For smooth compact signed $Q,P$, the
   243	  absolute correlation is compactly supported and bounded by $\|Q\|_2\|P\|_2$.
   244	  Local finiteness of $\Gamma$ therefore makes its physical integral finite.
   245	  Smooth signed covariance is positive: with the ordinary transform
   246	  $\widehat{Q}_{\mathrm{ord}}(\xi) = \int e^{i\xi\cdot x}Q(x)\ud x$, the model
   247	  convention gives
   248	  \[
   249	    B_\Gamma(Q,Q)=\int|\widehat{Q}_{\mathrm{ord}}(\xi)|^2\mu(\ud\xi)
   250	    \ge0,\qquad Q\in C_c^\infty(\R^d;\R).
   251	  \]
   252	  Pair $\Gamma$ with the smooth compact correlation to obtain this identity;
   253	  rapid Fourier decay and tempered $\mu$ give finiteness. Evenness of $\Gamma$
   254	  and $(x,y)\mapsto(x-y,-y)$ give symmetry. The quadratic polynomial for $Q+tP$
   255	  gives covariance Cauchy--Schwarz. In particular, for smooth real $f,h$,
   256	  \[
   257	    0\le B_\Gamma(f^2,h^2)
   258	    \le R_0N(f)^2N(h)^2.
   259	  \]
   260	  The squares of signed smooth profiles are already smooth and nonnegative.
   261	
   262	  Smooth compact functions are dense in $H^1$. Cutoffs equal to one on the
   263	  radius-$R$ ball, vanishing beyond $2R$ and with gradient at most $C/R$,
   264	  converge by the function and gradient tails and the bound $C\|f\|_2/R$ for the
   265	  extra gradient term. Mollification then converges in $H^1$ by $L^2$
   266	  translation continuity of the function and its weak gradients. The space is
   267	  separable through its closed isometric image $f\mapsto(f,\nabla f)$ in
   268	  $L^2(\R^d)^{d+1}$.
   269	
   270	  For arbitrary $f,h \in H^1$ take smooth approximants converging in $H^1$ and
   271	  along a common subsequence Lebesgue-a.e. Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-physical-pair}
   272	  transfers this convergence at both positions to $\nu$-a.e. convergence. Fatou
   273	  and continuity of $N$ give $B_\Gamma(f^2,h^2) \le R_0N(f)^2N(h)^2 < \infty$,
   274	  including the diagonal bound. At this stage Fatou supplies an inequality, not
   275	  continuity.
   276	
   277	  Apply ordinary Cauchy--Schwarz under the positive measure $\nu$ to
   278	  $f_1(x)f_3(x-y)$ and $f_2(x)f_4(x-y)$. The two squared integrals are finite by
   279	  the last bound; their square root is at most $R_0\prod_jN(f_j)$. This
   280	  proves~\eqref{E:spatial-four-linear}, absolute convergence and multilinearity.
   281	  Telescoping a difference one argument at a time and using $N(f) \le
   282	  \|f\|_{H^1}$ proves joint continuity. Thus, $A_{\mathrm{sp}}$ and the square
   283	  pairings are continuous. PSD for smooth compact profiles passes to finite
   284	  linear combinations of $H^1$ squares by this continuity, and its two-profile
   285	  Cauchy--Schwarz gives \eqref{E:spatial-square-CS}. This completes the physical
   286	  pairing argument beyond Fatou.
   287	
   288	  Every real unit $H^1$ profile has positive gradient energy by the Fourier
   289	  argument above. The homogeneous bound gives $R_{\mathrm{sp}} \le R_0$, and
   290	  smooth inclusion gives the reverse. Normalized smooth approximations preserve
   291	  the ratio by continuity. Finally, for nonzero $f$, choose a bounded set $E$ of
   292	  finite positive measure where $|f| \ge c > 0$. The correlation of $1_E$ is
   293	  continuous and positive near zero by $L^2$ translation continuity. An
   294	  origin-centered ball there has positive $\Gamma$ mass, so $A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f)
   295	  \ge c^4B_\Gamma(1_E,1_E) > 0$. This uses a nonnegative integral, not an $H^1$
   296	  claim for $1_E$. Finiteness was already proved. This proves
   297	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear}.
   298	\end{proof}

   304	    \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}

  3720	    \le B_r^{1/2}r^{-n},\qquad

  3760	  solution~\eqref{E:expansion}, constructed as a Stratonovich mild solution in

  3779	  \mathbb{Z}$, $t = 0,1/3,2/3$. They are nested: the difference between the
  3780	  parent and child shifts in child units is an integer, since $3t \in
  3781	  \mathbb{Z}$. For $s \ne r$ in $[0,T]$, choose a scale $3|s-r| < h_j \le

  3806	  Proposition~\ref{P:interval-coefficients}.
